newsitem.title: GERMANY: Debitel sees strong growth in German mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Debitel sees strong growth in German mobile phones.

text.p: German mobile communications group Debitel Kommunikationstechnik GmbH said on Tuesday it expected to achieve sales of 2.4 billion marks ($1.4 billion) this year, up from 1.77 billion marks in 1996.
Managing director Joachim Dreyer told reporters ahead of the CeBIT information technology fair in Hanover that the company's market share was around 17.3 percent in Germany at the end of last year.
The company, which is owned by German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG and retail giant Metro Holding AG, had 1.2 million subscribers at the end of 1996 and expects 1.574 million subscribers.
"I cannot give any details about our results, but let me say that we were not able to achieve our internal target of a three percent return on sales, but we were still above plan," Dreyer said.

Debitel currently generates around 20 percent of its sales outside of Germany with services in France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain and Austria. It claims around six percent of the French mobile phone market and 10.6 percent of the Dutch market.

In Germany, where the penetration of mobile communications has reached just 6.8 percent, Debitel expects the number of total mobile phone users to rise to 7.5 million this year, up from five million in 1996, and to 16 million in the year 2000.
"We see considerable growth opportunities for Debitel in this environment," said Dreyer.

Debitel does not operate its own communications network. Instead, it leases capacity from other operators and resells it with additional services. As a so-called "reseller", Debitel has become the third largest mobile communications company in Germany and one of the largest in Europe.
With the liberalisation of German and European telecommunications markets, Debitel also plans to begin offering resale services for fixed-wire long-distance calls for business.
The new service, called DirectLine, is the first simple resale service in Germany, a service that is now common in other countries such as the United Kingdom.

Debitel will install equipment at its customer's location that automatically routes any call over 200 km to a foreign carrier that is able to achieve savings of around 20 percent in charges for such long-distance calls.
"Large companies whose charges for international calls are more than 10,000 marks can save as much as 40 percent," Dreyer said.
The company would work together with RSL Com of the United States, a former subsidiary of Sprint Corp.
